# Portable research export 1.0.0

Read-only frozen research snapshot. Export policy `supervisor-acceptance-008/finishing-1` uses the current revision's supervisor acceptance, completion and output authorization. Acceptance permits stated limitations; it does not certify each finding, approve corpus mappings or establish an attack. Only `incidents` is the eligible population. `reference_incidents` are minimal provenance records, explicitly not approved for validated output. They never enter eligible counts, CSV rows or GeoJSON features.

## Files and relations

`manifest.json` lists schema/package/CSV/policy versions, exact build commit, generation time, dataset context, eligible IDs, counts, UTF-8 encoding, byte sizes and SHA-256 of every payload (excluding the manifest itself). `semantic_sha256` covers canonical sorted-key research JSON without generation metadata. ZIP uses uncompressed entries and fixed timestamps; unchanged data and metadata produce identical bytes. Generation time, app commit and explicitly labeled dataset context are generation metadata. Acceptance/history timestamps are recorded research, not generation metadata.

`research_export.json`: `incidents` (incident_id), `reference_incidents` (incident_id), `facilities` (facility_id), `incident_facilities` (incident_facility_id, incident_id, facility_id), `facts` (claim_id, incident_id, facility_id), `sources` (source_id), `fact_sources` (claim_source_id, claim_id, source_id), `tasks` (gap_task_id), `waivers`, bounded `history` and `disposition_history`. One incident may have several facilities; one fact may have several sources. Sources may address several facts. IDs remain original. Historical source-file/authority references and free-form dependency identifiers point outside this package where explicitly recorded; their bytes are not distributed. No inference of missing references, mapping approvals or research inputs occurs.

Facts carry family, exact `subject`, `scope`, raw `value`, shared `proposed_value`, derived `export_value`, `value_type`, `date_precision`, quantitative unit, impact basis, evidence state (`validation_state`), independent `lab_review_state`, review-needed flag, reviewer/time/revision, disposition/reason, waiver, current-value authority and historical research origin. Raw recorded values are retained even when the certified/exportable value is null. Null means unknown/not established, never false, zero or No. `SUPPORTED`, `NOT_SUPPORTED`, `CONFLICTING`, `NEEDS_MORE_EVIDENCE`, `NOT_APPLICABLE`, `NOT_REVIEWED` retain their original meanings. Lab states are `NOT_REVIEWED`, `REVIEWED`, `REOPENED`. Dispositions `ACTIVE`, `APPROVED`, `DEFERRED` are independent. Reasoned fact DEFER is a waiver, not factual certification. Tasks retain historical and current-lab state (`NOT_ASSESSED`, `ACTIVE`, `BLOCKED`, `DEFERRED`, `UNABLE_TO_RESOLVE`, `RESOLVED`) and remain nonblocking.

Each eligible incident includes truthful attack/context/unresolved classification, revision, approval reason/actor/time/policy, completion, acceptance readiness and limitations. Historical and current approval states remain distinct. Relevant activity before/after documents preserve earlier shared factual reviews; private drafts and command/session payloads are excluded.

Sources preserve recorded original/canonical URL or identifier, title, publisher/account, dates/access, locator, preservation references, limitations, social fields and legacy references. Evidence links retain `SUPPORTS`, `CONTRADICTS`, `LIMITS`, `CONTEXT_ONLY`, exact locators/excerpts/visual descriptions, originality/directness and dependency groups/provenance. Multiple dependent reports do not become independent confirmation by source count. A damage photograph supports damage, not service closure; evidence relationships address the exact proposition.

`incident_facilities.geojson` contains one Feature for every included incident–facility association, including historical links with `is_current:false` when recorded. It carries link ID, incident/facility IDs, relationship role, facility-match and classification plus coordinate provenance/review. Geometry is a Point using recorded facility longitude/latitude only; a first polygon vertex remains documented as such, not a surveyed centroid. Missing, nonnumeric or out-of-range coordinates produce geometry:null and a reason. Strike/event coordinates never substitute for facility geometry.

## CSV 2.0.0

`validated_incidents.csv` keeps the existing incident-per-row columns and adds `csv_schema_version`, `incident_facility_links_json`, `citations_json`. Existing `facts_and_provenance_json`, `facility_facts_and_provenance_json` and date-fact JSON also contain full per-finding citations. Each nested finding includes exact fact ID/family/proposition/scope, raw versus certified values, uncertainty/review/disposition/waiver, date precision/unit/basis, source IDs and complete citation objects. Every citation carries source ID/title/publisher/account/original and canonical URL verbatim, link direction/locator/excerpt, preservation, limitations and dependency metadata. Source-level versus link-level locators and limitations are separate. `url_status:MISSING_NOT_RECORDED` is explicit when no URL/identifier exists. `url_status:URL_UNAVAILABLE_PRESERVED_IDENTIFIER` distinguishes an identifier from an HTTP URL. Preserved identifiers are not invented HTTP URLs. Multiple sources are a JSON array, not a flattened ambiguous string.

UTF-8 CSV includes the existing leading BOM and uses comma delimiters, double quote escaping, and CRLF record delimiters; nested JSON must be parsed after CSV decoding. Empty scalar cells mean not established. Existing columns remain additive-compatible; consumers needing full provenance should accept version 2.0.0 and parse JSON arrays. Category counts use eligible incidents only; all associations are in the link JSON column and GeoJSON. CSV original single-primary-facility columns remain compatible; they do not imply a one-facility model.

## Verification and citation gaps

Run `python verify_export.py research-export-<version>.zip` in a clean directory using Python 3 standard library only. The verifier checks checksums/size/version, semantic digest, unique IDs, reference closure, CSV/JSON/GeoJSON agreement, multisite links, factual states, citations, geometry, waivers and counts. It writes reconstructed findings/citations and precise data-quality gaps to stdout as JSON. No database, application, network request or historical archive is needed.

Missing or historically malformed URLs, locators/excerpts, dates, values and coordinates are reported as data-quality gaps while retaining records. These do not change supervisor readiness or silently drop findings. Structural inconsistency or corruption introduced by an exporter fails verification. Recorded URLs/identifiers are never normalized or fabricated. URL reachability is not tested. The manifest is an integrity receipt, not a signature or guarantee of external source availability.
